- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f59304ddc45825f1f4d63f6956e07a75df68c9d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bf646ae246020f488000003aef460c46c4b3dd13` — the merge of head `3da7379b584bd9321d8eeed08360567fbb838103` into base `8f59304ddc45825f1f4d63f6956e07a75df68c9d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bf646ae246020f488000003aef460c46c4b3dd13 && git checkout bf646ae246020f488000003aef460c46c4b3dd13
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8f59304ddc45825f1f4d63f6956e07a75df68c9d 3da7379b584bd9321d8eeed08360567fbb838103 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8f59304ddc45825f1f4d63f6956e07a75df68c9d && git merge --no-ff 3da7379b584bd9321d8eeed08360567fbb838103

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8f59304ddc45825f1f4d63f6956e07a75df68c9d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8f59304ddc45825f1f4d63f6956e07a75df68c9d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3da7379b584bd9321d8eeed08360567fbb838103`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-organization-membership.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer0-verdict-on-operation.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-row-scope-declarations.test.ts + packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts (`vetOrganizationClaim`, `resolveUserAuthzGrants`, the session arm), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts (`resolveDelegatorContext`, `buildContextForUser`), packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/api-key.ts (posture classification), packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.ts, packages/runtime/src/security/resolve-execution-context.oauth-organization.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/errors.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/tenant-layer.ts, packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts, docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md (D10), docs/adr/0123-no-active-organization-session-semantics.md (D2)

Rendered at 2026-10-21T10:15Z, on card #25063's body and all five comments, PR #25101's body, file list and net diff from the merge base `4feccc268` (byte-identical to the three-dot diff against current `main`: 5 files, +379/−5), and the head's check-runs. Ruling of record: seat call `6312131621` (option P) and the widened claim `6311248489`. Disclosure (#9387, `5323310017`): this record states rules and abstract reach only.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) What is refused now that was accepted — confined to the ruled shape: right.** The one code change is a branch in `resolveOperationPrincipals`, inside the existing guard (the principal resolved at least one set, and the context carries the delegation link), on the `resolved` arm after the dangling-delegator refusal. It refuses when the context carries a non-empty active organization (`tenantId`) and `vetOrganizationClaim(liveOrganization, delegator.accessible_org_ids, this.tenancyPosture)` answers `undefined`. Read in `@objectstack/core`: that function returns the claim unchanged when the posture is absent or does not enforce a wall (`postureEnforcesWall` is `posture !== 'single'`), and otherwise answers the claim only while it is in the set. The set is the delegator's own: `buildContextForUser` resolves it through `resolveUserAuthzGrants`, which builds `accessible_org_ids` from the delegator's current `sys_member` rows, independent of the organization the grants are resolved in, and `resolveDelegatorContext` deliberately does not inherit it (ADR-0105 D2). So the refusal fires exactly for: a walled posture, a live active organization, a delegator whose membership does not back it — the ruled shape, no wider. It reaches both callers of the prologue: the engine middleware (every verb; a system context exits before it) and `checkControlledByParentWrite`, the attachment/comment parent gates, where the throw propagates unchanged as "a refusal of the context". The envelope is the existing `PermissionDeniedError` (`code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED'`, `status` and `statusCode` 403), its message opens with the `[Security] Access denied:` matcher prefix every transport maps to 403, and the developer message carries the `[ADR-0090 D10]` tag; no error code is added. What the rule refuses is what the card read: left to run, the delegator's leg could not bound the operation, because its own wall was built from the inherited organization (`isolated`) or excluded it (`group`) while a row that named no organization was placed in the live one. A delegated principal that resolves no set is not vetted here and is refused at object admission as before (ADR-0056 D2), so nothing the rule would refuse is admitted on that path. One precision note on the prose, not the code: "before any gate" is the file's idiom for the CRUD, capability, FLS, RLS and wall gates; the engine-owned write guard and the ADR-0090 D12 delegated-admin gate run ahead of the prologue, as they did.

**(b) The one real producer — judged from the code: no context the `/mcp` door builds is refused at the shipped default; right.** `assembleExecutionContext` sets the delegator to the authenticated user itself (`onBehalfOf.userId = authz.userId`) and the active organization to `authz.tenantId`. The runtime door hands the token's bound organization to the resolver as the synthetic session's active organization, and the session arm of `resolveAuthzContext` keeps `tenantId` only after `vetOrganizationClaim(tenantId, grants.accessible_org_ids, posture)` for that same user, with the posture classified by the same expression the plugin uses (`normalizeTenancyPosture(posture) ?? (isolationActive ? 'isolated' : 'single')`, core `api-key.ts` and `security-plugin.ts` alike). The prologue then asks the same function about the same user's membership-derived set, resolved fresh (`buildContextForUser` passes `bypassGrantsCache: true`). With the grants cache off, which is the shipped default (`OS_AUTHZ_GRANTS_CACHE_TTL_MS=0`), both answers come from the same `sys_member` read, so the door cannot build the refused shape; the producer's pin (`resolve-execution-context.oauth-organization.test.ts`, the real resolver into the real middleware under `isolated`) stays green by construction. The one exception is a non-default configuration: with the cache on, the door may answer from a cached envelope while the prologue answers fresh, so a membership that ended inside the TTL yields a context the door built and the prologue refuses. That is the fail-closed direction, and the seat call carries that window on this card ("refused by the same check"). The PR body's "every context the `/mcp` door builds" and the changeset's "never refused by this rule" hold at the default and are overstated by that window only.

**(c) The check calls `vetOrganizationClaim` and inlines nothing: right.** The import exists at the merge base (`security-plugin.ts:88`); the net diff adds no import, no helper, no membership test of its own and no posture test of its own. Only the consequence (refuse) is the prologue's, as the API-key arm's consequence is its own.

**(d) The three rewrites are honest, and each still pins what it pinned.** Pin 1 (`tenant-layer0-verdict-on-operation.test.ts`, the recorded intersection): the delegator's membership set now contains the live organization while still differing from the caller's; the two asserted walls and the recorded verdict moved consistently with that, and the verdict is still a set neither wall names alone, which is the subject (the recording line intersects, rather than recording the caller's half). Its control case takes the same memberships and drops only the link, so it is still the same fixture minus the link. Pin 2 (same file, the delegator with no membership): a delegator with no membership backs no organization, so no in-set move exists; the caller now carries no active organization, which the prologue has nothing to vet. Under `group` the caller's half of the wall reads the membership union, not the active organization, so that half is what it was, and the delegator's empty set still makes the composed wall `deny`: the subject (the composed wall fails closed, the caller's half does not) is intact. Keeping the organization and asserting the new refusal instead would have changed the subject and duplicated the new file. Pin 3 (`default-row-scope-declarations.test.ts`, the platform administrator's agent): the delegator gains membership in the organization every agent persona's request runs in; its leg is governed by the superuser bypass, which membership neither widens nor narrows, so the expected rows are unchanged and the letter-B reading (a ceiling's silence is not Layer 1 silence) is pinned as before. The fixture now models a platform administrator who is a member, where it modelled one who belonged to nothing acting in an organization: the shape the ruling refuses. Each rewrite is named in the PR body, as the seat call required.

**(e) The negative pins are ablation-verified: right, on the dev's run (not re-run here).** The method is sound: the first conjunct gates the whole refusal, so `false &&` on it through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` is the rule removed, with the direction predicted first and the restore proven by blob equality with HEAD. The predicted and observed red count, 16, is the file's refusal cells by construction (two walled postures × a public and a private object × four cells), and the file's design makes every refusal attributable to this rule alone: the delegator holds the private object's grant in the live organization too, so the D10 grant intersection cannot be what refuses, and the nine preservation cells pin the `single` posture, the no-active-organization context by ADR-0123 D2's own tag, the undelegated caller, the in-set delegated operation and the system context. The no-op `hook` that keeps `kernel:ready` from firing is stated in the file with its reason, and nothing the file pins reads what the platform bootstrap sets.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25063-delegated-organization-membership.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-security': minor`, a `fix(plugin-security)!:` title, the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line identical to the PR body's, exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and the BREAKING block (FROM, TO, Unchanged, the fix) in the #24813 shape. Level: right. A context that ran is refused and nothing widens, so this is a narrowing, BREAKING under 「甲」 rule 2 as amended (`6303865025`: a narrowing no conversion carries ships now, in 18.x, as a BREAKING minor); `skip-changeset` does not apply. Sentence by sentence against the code: the rule paragraph (the live organization, the delegator resolved in it on a stated assumption, nothing checked it, the prologue now checks it with `vetOrganizationClaim` under `isolated` or `group`) is true; the FROM is the pre-PR behaviour read in `resolveDelegatorContext` and the wall; the TO is the new branch's envelope; the Unchanged list is exact (the `single` posture, the no-active-organization context, a context without the link, the dangling delegator, system contexts); the fix sentence matches the branch (set `tenantId` to a backed organization, or leave it unset). Two precision notes, neither changing the level: "refused before any gate runs" reads as the file's idiom (the engine-owned write guard and the D12 gate precede the prologue), and "never refused by this rule" for the door's contexts holds at the default and is bounded by the grants-cache window (①b). The ADR-0087 arm is the honest one: no spec key, authorable spelling, object definition or stored shape moves, and no export is removed or narrowed (the diff adds one branch to a private method); the package publishes (no private flag, version 18.0.0); no ADR-0087 id is named. The PR does not edit ADR-0090, as the seat call required; the ADR's D10 text already states the rule the branch enforces.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **The dev's out-of-scope finding — paths that resolve a delegator without this refusal.** Judged in the cited code. Six are probes, diagnostics or explanations and are parity only, for the seat to file: `describeDelegationNarrowing` (decides nothing, never throws outward), `delegatedWriteContexts` (feeds plugin-sharing's per-record gate on the by-id write path, which only narrows, under a middleware whose prologue now refuses first), `resolveProjectionFieldMask` and `getReadableFields` (a column projection; the rows come through the middleware), `canReadObject`, `canWriteObject`, `canExport` (admission probes whose consumers then run the operation through the engine) and the explain engine. One is a data path and is escalated: `getReadFilter` → `computeDelegatedReadFilter`, the raw-SQL read-scope provider the analytics service bridges to (ADR-0021 D-C). It mirrors the middleware layer for layer but not its prologue: the delegator's leg is composed from the context `resolveDelegatorContext` rebuilds, whose Layer 0 input is the inherited active organization (`computeLayeredRlsFilter` reads `context.tenantId` and `context.accessible_org_ids`). Under `group` the delegator's union wall is its own membership set, so the live organization's rows are excluded. Under `isolated` the delegator's wall is the inherited live organization, so the provider answers a scope that admits that organization's rows where the middleware now refuses: the mechanism the card read, on a sibling door. Reach, abstractly: in-process only, the same population as the card; the analytics service receives the request's context from a door, and no door builds the shape. It does not make this PR's rule unsound for what the rule states and the ruling scoped (the engine's operation prologue, every verb), and it is pre-existing and unchanged by this diff; but it is not probe parity, because it serves rows, and it breaks the lock-step the provider's own doc promises between the find path and the raw-SQL path. The seat files it as its own card, ahead of the probe items; the mirror is one ask of the same function answering the deny sentinel, at the point the provider already mirrors the dangling-delegator refusal. No further detail here, per the disclosure ruling.
2. **`resolveDelegatorContext`'s same-organization comment** (`explain-engine.ts`, outside the surface): a pointer to the prologue check, not a rule; carried with the parity card. Answered.
3. **Deviations.** Pin 2's shape: judged honest in ①(d). `origin/main` moved after the merge base by four commits (spec, driver-turso, lint, the spec-shape gate); the diff of the merge base against current `main` over `plugin-security`, `core/src/security` and `runtime/src/security` is empty, so nothing this diff reads moved. Answered.
4. **The grants-cache window** (round-1 finding 1): carried by the ruling on this card; the code confirms the refusal there is fail-closed (①b). Answered.
5. **Fixture-realism drift** (round-1 finding 2): the new pin models the delegated principal as a user distinct from its delegator, which is the in-process population the rule targets, so it is apt here; the observation stands as noted, no card. Answered.
6. **`open_questions`:** none in the round-2 report; the round-1 question was answered by the seat call, and the PR implements option P as ruled (the prologue, no step 3.7, no `assertControlledByParentWrite`, no objectql, no spec, no ADR edit).
7. **Disclosure:** the card, the PR body, the changeset and this record carry rules and abstract reach only. The new pin file lands with the fix and pins the refusal, not the unfixed state.
8. **Check-runs on the head**, read at 2026-10-21T10:11Z: 40 runs. Green (27): Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, the three scoped lints, Type Check · source, consumer, debt ledger and workspace, TypeScript Type Check, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label, filter, and the four claim/card guards. Skipped (7, conditional or opt-in): Temporal Conformance, Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness. `pending` (6): Test Core (1/6), (2/6), (3/6), (4/6), (5/6), (6/6), the derived test family that holds the `plugin-security` suite. This verdict is the code's; a red shard re-opens it.

- This is the review of record for the claim `6311248489`, widened in place by the seat call `6312131621`.
- Contract review: owed on the narrowing face. **PASS** at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this same head (`6313542596`, isolated reviewer, `Local-runs: none`).
- ⛔ Disclosure (#9387, `5323310017`): this record states rules and abstract reach only.

1. **Form:**
   - The first line is `Fixes #25063`. The seat's grep finds no other closing keyword beside an issue number.
